annotation.method: Codex freshly reread the complete 55-page local paper, including every appendix result, compared each candidate with the frozen Mathlib and NumStability baselines, rejected the invented Appendix-A T2 formulation, and redesigned T3 to state Theorem 5.2's first-order conclusion without the former exact strengthening.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P16 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: published open-access journal version; IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis 46(4), 2026, printed pages 1939-1993

rejected_candidates.candidate: floating-point notation, gamma definition, condition numbers, singular values, and the forward-error definition in Section 2
rejected_candidates.reason: These are definitions or recalled standard tools; the backward-error identity built from them does not isolate a qualifying substantial library result.
They are assumptions of the framework rather than proved conclusions.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorem 3.1 full MOD-GMRES attainable forward/backward error theorem
rejected_candidates.reason: It is not selected as a separate task, but its modular perturbed-least-squares and residual argument is load-bearing in P16-T3's formalization of Theorem 5.2 rather than being supplied as an aggregate assumption.

Its modular coefficients depend on every operation model and on Theorem 3.1. The generic restart recurrence does not meet T2's two-result requirement, while P16-T3 targets the substantially harder MGS-GMRES argument that supplies a load-bearing correction result.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorems 5.1 and 5.3 for HH-GMRES and FGMRES
rejected_candidates.reason: These variants require separate Householder or flexible-preconditioning execution contracts. The MGS-specific Theorem 5.2 is selected because its loss-of-orthogonality and key-dimension argument supplies the stronger T3 challenge.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorems 6.1 and 6.2 for simpler GMRES and CGS2-GMRES
rejected_candidates.reason: Both require separate QR/Arnoldi/Gram-Schmidt execution contracts and singular-value rank arguments; Theorem 5.2 provides the paper's more detailed MGS loss-of-orthogonality proof.

A private neutral proof showed that its final recurrence is routine when correction-level and high-precision aggregate bounds are assumptions. Removing those assumptions makes the MGS-GMRES result of Theorem 5.2 the real hard dependency, so P16-T3 targets that dependency directly.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorems B.1, C.1, C.3, Lemma C.2, and Corollary C.4
rejected_candidates.reason: These appendix results require full finite QR/CGS2 implementations or polar/singular-value infrastructure not matched by the frozen library. The former P16-T2 was also removed because its arbitrary Givens-sequence statement was not a result stated in this paper.

rejected_candidates.candidate: prospective discussions of deflated, randomized, and block GMRES and all literature comparisons
rejected_candidates.reason: These are research directions, comparisons, or engineering guidance rather than completed universally quantified results of this paper.

T1.decision: Skipped: the candidate backward-error identity is assembled from standard finite-dimensional norm facts and does not isolate one qualifying NumStability result.

T2.decision: Skipped after strict source audit: the proof of Theorem A.1 cites Higham (2002), Theorems 19.10 and 8.5, for the Givens and triangular-solve bounds. The discarded target instead introduced a new arbitrary Givens-sequence Frobenius theorem not stated in this paper, so it was artificial rather than a faithful paper task.

T3.decision: Use Theorem 5.2's first-order MGS-GMRES backward-error conclusion at the selected key dimension, derived from stored Arnoldi, least-squares, correction-formation, and key-dimension data. NumStability has no corresponding GMRES result.

selection_policy: Use results proved in this paper and exact consequences of their displayed hypotheses, not empirical or prospective discussions.
Expose the paper's Euclidean/Frobenius normwise structure with finite-dimensional paper-scoped definitions.
For first-order claims, retain a source-supported higher-order semantics and keep the selected key dimension explicit; do not promote proof-specific exact strengthenings into the task statement.
Keep every public definition paper-scoped and free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only from the frozen library recorded in metadata/library_olean.json.
